findings.message: `_budget_refused` and its docstring assume the Claude adapter refuses the remaining-cap flag before a model turn, then `break` to a partial report. The run's engine log (.squatch/state/engine.log lines 128 and 259) contradicts this. The refused review calls at attempt 42 (run 1) and attempt 43 (run 2) took 6.4s and 3.1s, the same wall time as scored turns, and ended with 'Reached maximum budget'. That is what the CLI reports when a turn has already run past `--max-budget-usd`. The adapter's `parse` discards `total_cost_usd` on any error result, so both calls were journaled at usd 0.0. The ledger stops at 4.974945, but real spend is higher: ~0.1 was still left when each refused call started, so true spend likely went past the fixed USD 5.00 cap. That is the overflow the ticket's Definition of rejected names. `test_claude_remaining_cap_refusal_is_not_a_model_turn` only checks the string match, so it locks in the false premise without proving it.
findings.paved_road: Within the fence: make sure no review call starts unless the remaining budget covers a full review turn. For example, check before each fixture that remaining >= a per-review floor, such as the largest review cost journaled so far in this run. If it doesn't, break to the measured partial result through the existing `require_remaining` path. Then the CLI is never handed a budget it will overrun. Remove the `_budget_refused` break, or treat that outcome as Unscored. Replace its unit test with one showing the floor check stops before the call. File the adapter's dropped cost on error results (squatch/providers.py `parse`) to the Suggestion Box as a second problem, since that file is outside this fence.

findings.message: Two acceptance criteria are not met. The first says the harness 'executes once'. run.md says the first live invocation died at the cap refusal, and a second invocation 'resumed the same journaled run'. The engine log confirms two live runs, at 02:52 and 02:54, each with its own budget-refused call. The report's `spend_usd` (4.974945) leaves out both refused calls' unrecorded cost. So the second criterion, 'stays within USD 5.00', is not shown by the evidence and is probably false. Minor: `produced_at_sha` is the base commit 15255d4, so the report came from uncommitted code, not the committed head 4a2f379.
findings.paved_road: After fixing the pre-call floor, produce the report from one execution of the committed code whose journaled spend covers every provider call. State plainly in run.md that the earlier invocations spent money off-ledger, so the operator can see the real cost. Don't present the two-run result as a single execution under the cap.
